subject: Biotechnology
title: Terraforming with Biology
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Terraforming with Biology.

hook.text: Could engineered organisms make Mars breathable? Terraforming imagines seeding planets with life to transform their atmospheres.

buildup.text: Cyanobacteria oxygenated Earth 2.4 billion years ago — the Great Oxidation Event was biological terraforming of our own planet.

discovery.text: Engineered extremophiles could survive Martian soil — producing oxygen and breaking down perchlorates that make the soil toxic.

twist.text: Mars lacks a magnetic field — solar wind strips atmosphere faster than biology could rebuild it. Physics limits biology's power.

climax.text: Localized habitats with engineered biomes may be more realistic — enclosed ecosystems before open-air terraforming.

punchline.text: Life changed Earth — could it change Mars? Terraforming is biotech's grandest dream.

quiz.question: What physical barrier makes terraforming Mars with biology extremely difficult?
options: Mars is too far from the Sun for any organisms to survive
Mars lacks a magnetic field, so solar wind strips atmosphere faster than biology could produce it
Martian gravity is too strong for microorganisms to grow
